glosses: as far as; all the way to
patterns.usage_note: This まで is the complement that says how far an action reaches over a noun — of space, of time, or of degree — so it implies the whole span leading up to that point and the predicate is usually durative (待つ, 歩く, 続ける). Keep it apart from までに, which sets a deadline by which a one-shot event must happen: 五時まで待つ is waiting the whole time, 五時までに来る is arriving at some point before five. It is also not the limiting まで of 0304, which caps an allowance and shuts out anything beyond it (一人二枚まで), nor the range まで of 0301, which can take a whole verb clause (終わるまで) and yields the adnominal までの. In real Japanese this まで attaches to a plain-form verb too and pairs with から for an explicit start point; the corpus rule recorded here covers only the noun-attached use.

examples.ruby: 今日[きょう]は夕方[ゆうがた]まで図書館[としょかん]で調[しら]べ物[もの]をする。
examples.english: I'll be doing research at the library until early evening today.

examples.ruby: 駅[えき]までなら歩[ある]いて十分[じゅっぷん]もかからない。
examples.english: As far as the station it's not even a ten-minute walk.

examples.ruby: 荷物[にもつ]は玄関[げんかん]まで運[はこ]んでおきました。
examples.english: I've carried the bags as far as the entryway for you.
